The paper generalizes a previously introduced capillary-wave description of binary-alloy solidification to include the process of directional solidification.
A universal dispersion relation of the unstable eigenmodes of a planar steady-state solidification front is derived, which readjusts previously known stability considerations.
The paper establishes a differential equation for oscillatory motions of a planar interface that offers a limit-cycle scenario for the formation of solute bands and banded structures.
The model considers a class of systems with arbitrary equilibrium profiles of the solute concentration, which leads to an integro-differential equation for the interface position.
For a sufficiently small temperature gradient, the equation of motion can be reduced to the differential equation of a damped nonlinear oscillator.
Stationary solutions of the oscillator equation are shown to exist in some region, limited by the threshold of the Cahn instability.
The transition from uniform to periodic solutions near the stability threshold can be analytically evaluated using the Bogoliubov-Mitropolsky method.
The nature of the periodic solutions can be tuned from almost-harmonic to distinctive relaxation oscillations by changing the pulling velocity.
The inclusion of the inertial term in the oscillator equation is crucial, as it provides the necessary turnaround of trajectories at low velocities.
The temperature gradient determines the period of the limit-cycle solutions, with the bandwidth of the banded structures being inversely proportional to the gradient.
The generalized model presented in Appendix A includes energy density as an additional field variable and allows for finite heat conductivity.
The parameter m² acts as a long-wavelength cutoff for the Mullins-Sekerka instability and determines the period of the limit-cycle solutions.

Unlike previous phenomenological approaches, the present model derives the necessary turnaround of trajectories at low velocities from the inclusion of the inertial term, without requiring an ad hoc assumption of a hysteresis loop.
The Mullins-Sekerka instability enters the limit-cycle scenario in some parameter window, leading to the development of a dendritic microstructure in the low-velocity bands.
The almost stationary behavior of the interface motion in the low-velocity regime is barely understood and is complemented by the standard Mullins-Sekerka procedure.
